title: Directional commit tiers + enterprise SQ alignment pricing pilot
creator: Raj Patel
description: Objective: validate a directional-commit tiering model that decouples ingress/egress token rates for enterprise contracts while adding explicit guidance for answers to security questionnaires (SQs) about token metering, data residency, and billing transparency. Background: many enterprise prospects request line-item IO breakdowns in the security questionnaire and expect minimum-commit language in contracts. Current hosted pricing mixes IO into a single per-token price and uses flat minimums that create negotiation friction. This pilot will test whether: (1) offering committed tiers that specify separate ingress (input) and egress (output) rates improves acceptance velocity for enterprise SQs, (2) directional rebates for output-heavy workloads reduce sticker shock for embeddings/analysis customers, and (3) streaming sessions receive predictable microcredits instead of ambiguous streaming floors. Approach: create two new commit tiers (Commit-L and Commit-H) with directional IO splits, add a standard SQ appendix template describing metering and reconciliation, instrument telemetry to track acceptance rate, time-to-contract, churn, and cost-per-token. This ticket coordinates PM spec, legal appendix, pricing modeling, and telemetry + backend gating in billing service. Links: Confluence proposal: https://confluence.redwood.com/pricing/pm-91337-proposal | Pricing model workbook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pricing-models-2026 | GitHub PR for billing surface: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/1423 | Grafana probe: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ab12/pricing-probe
acceptance_criteria: Billing service supports separate ingress/egress rate fields and commit tiers for two pilot SKUs
Legal SQ appendix drafted and approved by Security & Legal
Telemetry dashboard shows token-level attribution (ingress vs egress) for pilot customers
Pilot launched to 8 targeted enterprise customers; we capture time-to-contract and acceptance feedback
A/B ramp plan exists and rollback guardrails documented
test_plan: Select 8 enterprise pilots from inbound SQ pipeline (mix of output-heavy embeddings customers and conversational customers)
Create three experiment cohorts: baseline (current pricing), commit-tier A (directional split 40/60), commit-tier B (directional split 20/80 with output rebate bands)
Expose pilot SKUs in customer console and via salesperson quote links; require SQ appendix included in OSC
Collect metrics for a 30-day window after contract signature: acceptance_rate, days_to_contract, monthly_recurring_value (MRV), usage_delta, billing_disputes
If any pilot customer reports >5% discrepancy in token attribution, pause and run reconciliation audit
metrics: Secondary: ARR uplift from commit thresholds
Secondary: per-token revenue differential (effective ingress/egress rates vs baseline)
rollout_steps: Week 0: finalize PM spec and legal SQ appendix (owner: Clara)
Week 1: implement backend support in billing API + QA (owner: ENG-billing team)
Week 2: enable telemetry + Grafana dashboards; create billing reconciliation job
Week 3: sales enablement and pilot onboarding (select 8 customers)
Week 4-8: monitor pilots, collect qualitative SQ feedback, iterate on appendix wording
Gate: decision point at week 8 to expand, adjust pricing math, or roll back
